items.title: Texas becomes the latest state to sue OpenAI
items.excerpt:
Similar to the lawsuits filed by Arizona, West Virginia, Iowa, and several others, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton accuses OpenAI of misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT, allegedly exposing children and other users to a “litany of harms” that’s “driven by the company’s insatiable quest to win the AI arms race and amass
large fortunes.”
[Link: Texas AG Sues OpenAI, Altman for Negative Effects on Consumers | https://news.bloomberglaw.com/privacy-and-data-security/texas-ag-sues-openai-altman-for-negative-effects-on-consumers | Bloomberg Law]

items.title: Chancellor unveils Britain's ambitious plan for AI
items.excerpt: Major package to unlock the opportunities of AI in every postcode, scale up home grown AI firms, and keep UK safe from threats announced by the Chancellor.

items.title: As the US and China form AI blocs, countries are increasingly torn between them
items.excerpt: With the US-led Pax Silica and the China-inspired World AI Cooperation Organization forming rival AI blocs, other countries such as Kazakhstan are trying to bridge both; experts say the window to choose freely between US chips and China's cheaper open-source AI may be narrowing.

items.title: Treasury Department proposes curbs on high-tech investments, including AI, in China, Russia, North Korea
items.excerpt: Treasury proposed a rule expanding the Outbound Investment Security Program to cover US investments over $50,000 in AI, HPC, quantum, hypersonics and biotech in China, Russia, North Korea and other countries of concern, implementing the 2025 COINS Act.

items.title: China's MiniMax completes export registration for open-source, overseas AI model licensing
items.excerpt: MiniMax said it completed technology export registration with China's commerce ministry for open-source release and overseas licensing of certain models, a week after Beijing proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies including models, agents and computing clusters.

items.title: DeepSeek and MiniMax cleared to take AI models abroad, state media says
items.excerpt: Under China AI export controls, “AI companies can continue with their commercialization efforts as usual,” a CCTV-linked account says.

items.title: Nvidia B300 chips reportedly surface on China Telecom-linked network, raising export-control questions
items.excerpt: Israeli security firm Lava identified 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs through monitoring endpoints linked to China Telecom, a state-owned carrier. The chips are barred from sale to China under US export controls. The finding adds to questions about whether the restrictions can keep advanced AI processors out of the country, but the network data does not establish where the GPUs are physically located.

items.title: Did the United States and Russia Just Agree to Collaborate on Data Centers?
items.excerpt: CSIS analyzes a joint US-Russia data center proposed as part of broader negotiations, arguing it poses a substantive threat to US national security.

items.title: Washington's message to AI execs: please shut up
items.excerpt: Lawmakers and White House advisers tell Axios that AI leaders' focus on digital sentience and catastrophe is becoming a political liability that complicates the regulatory debate.

items.title: What the US Movement Against Data Centers Can Learn From Abroad
items.excerpt: Paris Marx, author of Hyperscale, has been tracking global data center development for years. The US has a lot to learn from what’s happened everywhere from Ireland to New Zealand.

items.title: Want to build a UK datacenter? Please hold while Whitehall transfers you
items.excerpt: Minister insists responsibilities are clear as construction, telecoms, and energy fall under separate departments

items.title: A Congressional Commission on AI Risk is Overdue
items.excerpt: As AI leaders sound the alarm about high stakes and a closing window for regulation, Zoë Baird says there is historic precedent for a congressional commission.

items.title: Opposition deepfake video of Spanish PM's wife sparks outrage before election
items.excerpt: Video shows AI likenesses of people linked to Pedro Sánchez’s Socialist party appearing to admit to wrongdoing

items.title: Russian disinformation group targets James Talarico with baseless claim in AI-generated video
items.excerpt: Researchers say a fake video accusing Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico of sexual misconduct is the latest example of Russian groups generating false information to influence U.S. elections.

items.title: AI 데이터센터 건립 문턱 낮춘다… 내년 기술 실증에 2000억 투입
